doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Choosing lyrics that tell a story
summary: She picks lyrics that tell stories and address her own life, and feels humble to do her work.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. The songs that you sang tonight, all of them were profound. They were gripping. Much of the music that I hear in the pop world today is so surface. And even if it were to be sung well it wouldn’t mean much because the lyrics don’t take me anywhere. What in a set of lyrics attracts you to say yes I’d like to sing that song?

I like lyrics that tell a story, that have very, very, that really, really kind of most of the songs really address my own life, things that I really think about, that I think that I can give my own emotion and understanding to, so that the audience understands it more the way that I’m hearing it, more than maybe the way the person wrote it. Also I think just, it really all comes down to just really feeling very humble, to be able to have the opportunity to do what it is that I do. I think that’s the greatest thing.
